stories.title: Investigation into killing of Hind Rajab and Gaza paramedics comes ‘extremely late’
stories.summary: The investigation into the killing of Hind Rajab and paramedics in Gaza launched by the Israeli army came as a “surprise” in the country, “because so much time has passed” since the events took place, FRANCE 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky said. “The timing is extremely late.” But Tarnopolsky said “the fact that these two very renown cases are being referred to criminal investigation is already an admission on the part of the Israeli army that something here went deeply wrong.”

stories.title: Suspense thriller 'Mousetrap' reinvents Korean folktale: director
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 20 (Yonhap) -- The upcoming Netflix original series "Mousetrap" draw...
article_sentences: The upcoming Netflix original series "Mousetrap" draws inspiration from a Korean folktale in which a rat turns into a person by eating that person's clipped nails, while weaving in a chase to track down the rat-turned-human, its director said Thursday.

Based on the webtoon "Field Mouse," it follows Moon-jae (Ryu Jun-yeol), a reclusive writer who finds himself robbed of his identity and becomes embroiled in a high-stakes hunt to track down the "rat" that seems to know him even better than he knows himself.
The 10-episode series also features Sul Kyung-gu as Noja, a loan shark who teams up with Moon-jae to track down the rat, and Lee Kyoo-hyung as a police detective involved in the mysterious case.
"It is a story inspired by the traditional folktale of a field mouse who eats clipped nails," director Kim Hong-sun said at a press conference.
"It is a thriller in which a person whose life has been completely taken away seeks to regain his identity."
To differentiate the series from other works that explore themes of stolen identities and truth, Kim said he made the process of tracking down the rat central to the plot.
While the story does not feature heroes with superpowers, the lead actors said they were drawn to the plot of losing and regaining one's identity and questioning what is real in the process.
"The characters are not superheroes, they are actually very normal people.
The plot centers on the uneasiness, the fear and doubt the characters go through, exploring what it means to be true, to be real," Sul said.
Ryu, who said he read the webtoon before reading the full script, said the original work asks readers how a person's identity can be understood and proven.
"The original webtoon is very deep and philosophical.
I think what it wanted to ask was how we can be defined and proven, whether that is our true self and whether the people we see are also their true selves," he said.
